title: Position: Irresponsible AI: big tech’s influence on AI research and associated impacts
claim: A dominant industrial actor shapes a research ecosystem and produces harms, while critical, open, community-oriented alternatives offer a path forward.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right landscape; hand-drawn metaphor scene with smokestacks to ivory tower
description: A single wide, hand-drawn sketch in black line art with red and blue handwritten labels. On the left, large factory smokestacks labeled BIG TECH and CAPITALISM emit clouds labeled military impacts, mis/disinformation and ethical impacts. A construction crane is labeled 'scale thinking', an oil derrick sits above a pit labeled environmental harm with dead fish, and critical workers peek out from a small shelter. In the middle, a van carrying funding and scientific papers and a bus labeled 'AI talent' travel a road under a blue ribbon labeled TECHNOLOGY toward the right. On the right, a castle labeled AI RESEARCH has a gatekeeper, an 'academic openness' door, a person with a telescope ('critical lens') and an 'ivory tower'. Below it are an AI co-op sustainable garden and a 'science for the people' stall. The eye goes first to the large BIG TECH lettering.
caption: An artistic summary of our position, depicting certain aspects of the influence of big tech in AI research, its associated impacts, and our call to action.
abstract: The accelerated development, deployment and adoption of artificial intelligence systems has been fuelled by the increasing presence of big tech in the AI field. This trend has been accompanied by growing ethical concerns and intensified societal and environmental impacts. This position paper argues that irresponsible AI development is strongly driven by big tech's influence and involvement in the field. First, we examine the growing and disproportionate influence of big tech in AI research and argue that its drive for scaling and general-purpose systems is fundamentally at odds with the responsible, ethical, and sustainable development of AI. Second, we review key current environmental and societal negative impacts of AI and trace their connections to big tech's influence. Third, we discuss the underlying economic forces driving big tech's actions. Finally, as a call to action, we invite AI researchers to counter big tech's influence in irresponsible AI development through strategies that build on the responsibility of implicated actors and collective action.
